questions.question: Find the value of [(12 times 10) timesleft{6 div 6 times ((15-12))/(3)right}]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Expression to solve: [(12 times 10) timesleft{6 div 6 times ((15-12))/(3)right}] 

 

**Formula Used:**

Follow BODMAS (Bracket, Order, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction) rules to simplify the expression.

**Calculation:**

[(12 times 10) timesleft{6 div 6 times ((15-12))/(3)right}] 

⇒ [(12 times 10) timesleft{6 div 6 times ((3))/(3)right}] 

⇒ [(120) timesleft{1 times 1right}] 

⇒ 120

**The value of the expression is 120.**

questions.question: Anil has ₹1224 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Ashok and Raj and asked them to invest it at 4% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Ashok and Raj got same amount after 13 and 14 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Anil give to Raj?

When amounts are equal under CI, the ratio of principals is determined by the rate and time difference.

Ratio of Ashok's share to Raj's share = (100 + R)/100 : 1 = 104 : 100 = 26 : 25.

Total ratio parts = 26 + 25 = 51 parts.

Raj gets 25 parts because his money is invested for a longer period (14 years vs 13 years).

Raj's share = (25 / 51) × 1224 = 25 × 24 = ₹600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 15 days and B can do it in 24 days. If they do the work alternately, in how many days will they finish the work, provided that A begins the work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(15, 24) = 120 units.

Efficiency of A = 120 ÷ 15 = 8 units/day, Efficiency of B = 120 ÷ 24 = 5 units/day.

Work done in the first 2 days (A + B) = 8 + 5 = 13 units.

Work done in 18 days (9 alternating pairs) = 13 × 9 = 117 units.

Remaining 3 units are done by A on the 19th day in 3/8 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 ³/₈ days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 15 days

Time taken by B = 24 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 **Efficiency**

**Calculations:**

⇒ In alternate working, A works on Day 1, B works on Day 2.

⇒ Work done in 2 days = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B = 8 + 5 = 13 units.

⇒ Multiply by 9 to get close to the total work: 13 × 9 = 117 units.

⇒ Time taken for 117 units = 2 × 9 = 18 days.

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Work done = 120 − 117 = 3 units.

⇒ On the 19th day, it is A's turn to work.

⇒ Time taken by A to complete the remaining work = 3 ÷ 8 days.

⇒ Total time taken = 18 + ³/₈ = 18 ³/₈ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 ³/₈ days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work

When people work on alternate days, calculate the combined work of one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and find how many full cycles fit into the total work before assigning remaining work to the starter.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual total work done by each person. If they work together for the same number of days, wages are distributed exactly in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns

Works on the same concept as Time & Work. The only major difference is that an outlet or leakage pipe does negative work, which subtracts from the total combined efficiency.
</p

questions.question: The average weight of Atul, Baban and Rakesh is 46 kg. If the average weight of Atul and Baban be 39 kg and that of Baban and Rakesh be 50 kg , then the weight of Baban (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weight of Baban = (Total weight of Atul & Baban) + (Total weight of Baban & Rakesh) − (Total weight of all three)

Weight of Baban = (39 × 2) + (50 × 2) − (46 × 3)

Weight of Baban = 78 + 100 − 138

Weight of Baban = 178 − 138 = 40 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 40 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of Atul, Baban, and Rakesh = 46 kg

Average weight of Atul and Baban = 39 kg

Average weight of Baban and Rakesh = 50 kg

**Formula Used:**

Total sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the weights of Atul, Baban, and Rakesh be A, B, and R respectively.

⇒ Total weight of all three (A + B + R) = 46 × 3 = 138 kg

⇒ Total weight of Atul and Baban (A + B) = 39 × 2 = 78 kg

⇒ Total weight of Baban and Rakesh (B + R) = 50 × 2 = 100 kg

⇒ Adding both pairs together gives us the weight of everyone, but Baban is counted twice:

⇒ (A + B) + (B + R) = 78 + 100

⇒ A + 2B + R = 178 kg

⇒ Subtracting the total weight of all three from the equation above:

⇒ B = (A + 2B + R) − (A + B + R)

Inclusion-Exclusion in Averages

When sub-groups overlap, the value of the overlapping entity is determined using the logic: Overlapping Value = (Sum of partial group totals) − (Overall total).

Weighted Average

If group 1 has n₁ items with an average of A₁, and group 2 has n₂ items with an average of A₂, the combined average is calculated as (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Deviation Method for Averages

The algebraic sum of the deviations of a set of values from their arithmetic mean is always equal to zero. This principle provides a faster route for missing or replaced values in a series.

questions.question: When 7516, 7635 and 7992 are divided by the greatest number x, then the remainder in each case is the same. The product of the digits of x is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The greatest number leaving the same remainder is the HCF of their absolute differences.

Differences = (7635 − 7516), (7992 − 7635), (7992 − 7516) = 119, 357, 476.

x = HCF(119, 357, 476) = 119.

Product of digits of x = 1 × 1 × 9 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 7516, 7635, and 7992.

**Formula Used:**

The greatest number x that divides given numbers a, b, and c leaving the same remainder is given by x = HCF(|a − b|, |b − c|, |c − a|).

**Calculations:**

⇒ |a − b| = 7635 − 7516 = 119

⇒ |b − c| = 7992 − 7635 = 357

⇒ |c − a| = 7992 − 7516 = 476

⇒ x = HCF(119, 357, 476)

⇒ We can observe that 357 = 119 × 3 and 476 = 119 × 4.

⇒ Hence, the HCF of 119, 357, and 476 is 119, meaning x = 119.

⇒ We need the product of the digits of x.

⇒ Product of digits = 1 × 1 × 9 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Numbers with Different Remainders

When finding the greatest number dividing a, b, c and leaving remainders r₁, r₂, r₃ respectively, the required number is HCF(a − r₁, b − r₂, c − r₃).

LCM of Numbers Leaving the Same Remainder

To find the smallest number which when divided by x, y, and z leaves the same remainder r in each case, the number is LCM(x, y, z) + r.

Difference Property of HCF

The HCF of any set of numbers is always a factor of their absolute differences. This property simplifies finding the HCF of large numbers by focusing on evaluating the smallest difference between them.
</p

questions.question: The greatest number that will divide 42, 84 and 153 so as to leave the same remainder in each case is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the greatest number that leaves the same remainder, take the HCF of their absolute differences.

Differences: |84 − 42| = 42, |153 − 84| = 69, |153 − 42| = 111.

Required number = HCF of (42, 69, 111).

HCF(3 × 14, 3 × 23, 3 × 37) = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 42, 84 and 153.

**Formula Used:**

The greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder in each case is given by the HCF of |x − y|, |y − z| and |z − x|.

**Calculations:**

⇒ First difference = |84 − 42| = 42

⇒ Second difference = |153 − 84| = 69

⇒ Third difference = |153 − 42| = 111

⇒ Now, we need to find the HCF of 42, 69, and 111.

⇒ Prime factorization of 42 = 2 × 3 × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 69 = 3 × 23

⇒ Prime factorization of 111 = 3 × 37

⇒ The common factor among all three numbers is 3.

⇒ HCF(42, 69, 111) = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Greatest number leaving same unknown remainder

When a number divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder, the required greatest number is the HCF of |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

Greatest number leaving specific remainders

The greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving remainders a, b, and c respectively is the HCF of (x − a), (y − b), and (z − c).

Least number leaving same remainder

The smallest number which when divided by x, y, and z leaves the same remainder r in each case is given by LCM(x, y, z) + r.

Least number leaving different remainders

If divided by x, y, z leaving remainders a, b, c where (x − a) = (y − b) = (z − c) = k, the required number is LCM(x, y, z) − k.
</p

questions.question: A number is increased by 50% and then again by 50%. By what percentage should the increased number be reduced so as to get back the original number?

Successive increases of 50% mean multiplying by the fraction (1 + 1/2) = 3/2 twice.

Final value = Original value × (3/2) × (3/2) = Original × (9/4).

This means if the original number is 4, it becomes 9.

To restore the original number, the final value 9 must be reduced by 5.

Required percentage reduction = (5 ÷ 9) × 100 = 500/9 % = 55 5/9 %.

Third Proportional

Fourth Proportional

Duplicate & Sub-duplicate Ratios

questions.question: Akshay has ₹1218 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Arjun and Kartik and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Arjun and Kartik got same amount after 12 and 13 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Akshay give to Kartik?

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 26 cm and its length is 7 cm. Find its area in cm².
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of length and breadth = Perimeter ÷ 2 = 26 ÷ 2 = 13 cm.

Since the length is 7 cm, the breadth is 13 − 7 = 6 cm.

Area = length × breadth = 7 × 6 = 42 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 42 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of the rectangle = 26 cm

Length (l) = 7 cm

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter = 2(l + b)

Area = l × b

 
 Length (l) = 7 cm
 Breadth (b) = 6 cm
 Area = ?

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2(l + b) = 26

⇒ 7 + b = 13

⇒ b = 13 − 7 = 6 cm

⇒ Area = l × b

⇒ Area = 7 × 6 = 42 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 42 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The length of the diagonal d of a rectangle can be calculated using the formula d = √(l² + b²).

Square Properties

A square is a special type of rectangle where all four sides are equal (length = breadth = a). Its Perimeter = 4a and Area = a².

Area of Four Walls of a Room

Also known as the lateral surface area of a cuboid, it is calculated as Area = 2(l + b) × h, where h is the height of the room.
</p

questions.question: On a circular path of 432 m, Soham and Rohan start running from the same point and in same direction at the speed of 12 m/sec and 9 m/sec, respectively. Find the time in which they will meet for the first time.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in the same direction = Speed of Soham − Speed of Rohan

Relative speed = 12 − 9 = 3 m/sec

Time for first meeting = Path Length ÷ Relative speed

Time = 432 ÷ 3 = 144 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 144 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Start Point
 
 Distance = 432 m
 
 

 Soham: 12 m/sec
 
 

 Rohan: 9 m/sec

**Given:**

Length of the circular path = 432 m

Speed of Soham = 12 m/sec

Speed of Rohan = 9 m/sec

**Formula Used:**

When running in the same direction, relative speed = Speed₁ − Speed₂

Time to meet = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative speed of Soham and Rohan = 12 − 9 = 3 m/sec

⇒ Time required for their first meeting = 432 ÷ 3

⇒ Time = 144 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 144 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting at the Starting Point

To find the time when the runners will meet specifically at the starting point, calculate the LCM (Least Common Multiple) of the times taken by each individual to complete exactly one full round.

Meeting Anywhere (Opposite Directions)

If two runners move in opposite directions, their relative speed becomes the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). The time of their first meeting is Path Length ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

When two individuals run on a circular track with speeds 'a' and 'b' (expressed in simplest ratio form), the number of distinct points they meet at is |a − b| for the same direction and (a + b) for opposite directions.
</p

questions.question: Two trains having lengths of 300 m and 200 m are running at speeds of 70 km/h and 120 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Distance = 300 + 200 = 500 m = 0.5 km

Relative Speed (same direction) = 120 − 70 = 50 km/h

Time (hours) = Distance ÷ Speed = 0.5 ÷ 50 = 1/100 hours

Time (minutes) = (1/100) × 60 = 0.6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 0.6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of slower train (L₁) = 300 m

Speed of slower train (S₁) = 70 km/h

Length of faster train (L₂) = 200 m

Speed of faster train (S₂) = 120 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time taken to cross = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₂ − S₁

questions.question: Find the value of [(14 times 9) timesleft{8 div 2 times ((18-15))/(3)right}]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Expression to solve = [(14 × 9) ×left{8 div 2 × ((18-15))/(3)right}] 

**Formula Used:**

Follow BODMAS (Brackets, Orders, Division/Multiplication, Addition/Subtraction).

**Calculation:**

[(14 × 9) ×left{8 div 2 × ((18-15))/(3)right}] 

⇒ [(126) ×left{4 × (3)/(3)right}] 

⇒ 126 × 4

⇒ 504

**The value of the expression is 504.**

questions.question: 400 mangoes were bought at ₹1210 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹960. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of mangoes.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Cost Price (CP) for 400 mangoes = 4 × 1210 = ₹4840

Total Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = 4840 + 960 = ₹5800

Selling Price per dozen = (Total SP ÷ Total Mangoes) × 12

Selling Price per dozen = (5800 ÷ 400) × 12 = 14.5 × 12 = 174

**∴ The correct answer is ₹174.**

questions.question: The time period of a simple pendulum is found to be 2.2 sec, 1.8 sec, 2 sec, 1.6 sec and 2.4 sec. What is the average time period (in sec)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the assumed average be 2.0 sec.

Deviations of values from 2.0 are: +0.2, −0.2, 0, −0.4, +0.4.

Sum of deviations = 0.2 − 0.2 + 0 − 0.4 + 0.4 = 0.

Actual Average = Assumed Average + (Sum of deviations ÷ n) = 2.0 + (0 ÷ 5) = 2.0 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time periods = 2.2 sec, 1.8 sec, 2 sec, 1.6 sec, 2.4 sec

Total number of observations = 5

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of time periods = 2.2 + 1.8 + 2.0 + 1.6 + 2.4

⇒ Sum = 10 sec

⇒ Average = 10 ÷ 5 = 2 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 2 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The arithmetic mean is the sum of a collection of numbers divided by the count of numbers in the collection.

Deviation Method

For simple calculations, assume a middle value as the average. The net deviation of all terms from this assumed average divided by total terms gives the required adjustment to find the actual average.

Time Period of a Simple Pendulum

The time taken for one complete oscillation is given by T = 2π√(L ÷ g), where L is the length of the string and g is the acceleration due to gravity.

questions.question: The price (per litre) of petrol increases by 75%. By what percent should its consumption be reduced such that the expenditure on it increases by 47% only?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial expenditure and price base be 100 units.

If consumption remains unchanged, the new expenditure after a 75% price hike will be 175.

However, the allowed new expenditure is only 147 (due to a maximum 47% increase).

Required reduction on the new price base = 175 − 147 = 28.

Percentage reduction in consumption = (28 ÷ 175) × 100 = 16%.

**∴ The correct answer is 16%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 100
 Initial
 
 
 175
 Price Base

 
 147
 New Exp

 

 + 75% (Price Increase)

 

 + 47% (Exp Limit)

 
• 
 −28
 Reduction
 
 Reduction = 16%

**Given:**

Price increase = 75%

Expenditure increase = 47%

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial price be ₹100 and initial consumption be 100 units.

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 × 100 = ₹10,000

⇒ New Price = ₹100 + 75% of 100 = ₹175

⇒ New Expenditure = ₹10,000 + 47% of 10,000 = ₹14,700

⇒ New Consumption = New Expenditure ÷ New Price

⇒ New Consumption = 14,700 ÷ 175 = 84 units

⇒ Reduction in consumption = Initial Consumption − New Consumption

⇒ Reduction in consumption = 100 − 84 = 16 units

⇒ Percentage reduction = (16 ÷ 100) × 100% = 16%

**∴ The correct answer is 16%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Price, Consumption & Expenditure Relation

Expenditure = Price × Consumption. If Expenditure is constant, Price and Consumption are inversely proportional to each other.

Percentage Change

Percentage Change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. It measures the relative magnitude of change compared to the original base value.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is subjected to two consecutive percentage changes of a% and b%, the effective net percentage change is given by the formula: a + b + (a × b ÷ 100)%.
